messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Fast fourier transform
messages.body_plain:
Thanks a lot Kasper. I am interested in both the real and the imaginary parts. I added:

struct FFTTransformer {
  template <class Mat>
  Mat apply_fft(const Mat& X) {

    Mat X_transformed(X.rows(), 2 * X.cols()); // first half are real, next half imaginary

Eigen::FFT<Type> fft;
    for (int i = 0; i < X.rows(); i++) {
      Eigen::Array<std::complex<Type>, Eigen::Dynamic, 1> fft_result(X.cols());
      Eigen::Array<Type, Eigen::Dynamic, 1> Xrow = X.row(i);
      fft.fwd(fft_result.data(), Xrow.data(), X.cols());

  for (int j = 0; j < X.cols(); j++){
X_transformed(i,j) = fft_result[j].real();
X_transformed(i,X.cols() + j) = fft_result[j].imag();
  }
    }
    return X_transformed;
  }
};

and it worked fine.

Thanks a lot for your help!!

Mike

messages.subject: Efficient v * M^{-1} where M is sparse and asymmetric?
messages.subject_clean: Efficient v * M^{-1} where M is sparse and asymmetric?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Does anyone know an efficient way in TMB to compute  where  is a large, square, sparse, asymmetric matrix and  is a vector (i.e., without forming  in memory)?

It seems like R-package Matrix can do this using a "sparseQR" decomposition (presumably using options that are also in the Eigen package), but I don't see this functionality documented <https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/> in TMB.

Cheers,
Jim

messages.subject: Re: Efficient v * M^{-1} where M is sparse and asymmetric?
messages.subject_clean: Efficient v * M^{-1} where M is sparse and asymmetric?
messages.body_plain:
Eigen has both sparse LU and sparse QR.

Here an example with LU:

#include <TMB.hpp> template<class Type> Type objective_function<Type>::operator() () { DATA_SPARSE_MATRIX(M); PARAMETER_VECTOR(y); Eigen::SparseLU< Eigen::SparseMatrix<Type>, Eigen::COLAMDOrdering<int> > lu; lu.compute(M); matrix<Type> x = lu.solve(y.matrix()); REPORT(x); return x.array().sum(); }
​

## Data and parameters set.seed(1) n <- 1e4 M <- Matrix::bandSparse(n, k=-1:1,diag=list(rnorm(n-1),rnorm(n),rnorm(n-1))) y <- rnorm(n) data <- list(M=M) parameters <- list(y=y) ## Make a function object obj <- MakeADFun(data, parameters) ## Test obj$fn(y) sum(solve(M,y))
​

The approach has the usual downside when taping algorithms, that it might use parameter dependent branching internally. Also, it's not as fast as an atomic sparse LU would be.
